chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Is'haq, from Abdullah ibn Hammad, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
When the shares are drawn (lots), the (right of) pre-emption is lifted.

key_terms.السِّهَامُ: The lots or shares drawn to determine order or allocation.
key_terms.الشُّفْعَةُ: The right of pre-emption, allowing a partner or co-owner to buy out another's share.

ai.seo_question: When does the right of pre-emption (shuf'ah) end in Islamic law?
ai.summary: In the context of Shia jurisprudence, this hadith clarifies the temporal boundary of the right of pre-emption (shuf'ah), indicating that the procedural act of drawing lots (qur'a) finalizes the allocation and extinguishes the co-owner's priority claim. This ruling underscores the importance of procedural certainty in property transactions, ensuring that once the distribution mechanism is initiated, the legal status of shares becomes fixed. It reflects the scholarly emphasis on minimizing disputes among partners by defining clear moments when rights transition from potential to actualized.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from Ibrahim Bin Is’haq, from Abdullah Bin Hammad, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When the shares are drawn (lots), the (right of) pre-emption is lifted’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq from ‘Abd Allah ibn Hammad from Jamil ibn Darraj from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
When division takes place, al-Shuf ’ (one’s rights of pre- emption) ceases to apply.’”
